==English==
{{wp}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|registre||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
From {{der|en|la-med|registrum}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|regesta||list, items recorded}}, from {{der|en|la|regero|regerō|to record, to carry back}}, from {{m|la|re-}} + {{m|la|gero|gerō|t=to carry, bear}}. Compare {{cog|la|registoria||a treasurer}}. Some senses influenced by association with unrelated {{noncog|la|rego|regō|to rule}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɹɛd͡ʒ.ɪ.stə/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɹɛd͡ʒ.ɪ.stɚ/|/ˈɹɛd͡ʒ.ə.stɚ/|a=GA,CA}}
** {{audio|en|En-us-register.ogg|a=California}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɹed͡ʒ.ɪ.stə/|a=AU}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɹed͡ʒ.ə.stə/|a=NZ}}
* {{hyphenation|en|re|gis|ter}}

===Noun===
{{wikidata lexeme|L18026}}
{{en-noun}}

# A [[formal]] [[recording]] of [[names]], [[events]], [[transactions]], etc.
#: {{ux|en|The teacher took the '''register''' by calling out each child's name.}}
# A [[book]] of such entries.
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merry Wives|II|ii|passage=As you have one eye upon my follies, {{...}} turn another into the '''register''' of your own.}}
# An [[entry]] in such a book.
# The [[act]] of registering.
# A [[certificate]] issued by the collector of customs of a port or district to the owner of a vessel, containing the description of a vessel, its name, ownership, and other material facts. It is kept on board the vessel, to be used as evidence of nationality or as a [[muniment]] of title.
# One who registers or records; a [[registrar]]; especially, a public officer charged with the duty of recording certain transactions or events.
#: {{ux|en|a '''register''' of deeds}}
# A [[distinct]] [[horizontal]] (or, more rarely, [[vertical]]) [[section]] of a [[work of art]] or [[inscription]] that is [[divide]]d into several such sections.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2005|author=Abeer El-Shahawy|title=The Egyptian Museum in Cairo: A Walk Through the Alleys of Ancient Egypt|page=23
|passage=The reverse side is divided into three '''registers'''. In the first '''register''' is the name of Narmer represented as a fish and a chisel inscribed in the ''serekh''.}}
# A [[device]] that [[automatically]] records a [[quantity]].
# {{lb|en|telecommunications}} The part of a [[telegraphic]] [[apparatus]] that automatically records the message received.
# {{lb|en|telecommunications}} A list of received calls in a [[phone set]].
# {{lb|en|computing}} A small unit of very [[fast]] [[memory]] that is directly [[accessible]] to the [[central processing unit]], and is mostly used to [[store]] [[input]]s, [[output]]s{{,}} or [[intermediate]] [[result]]s of [[computation]]s.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1992|author=Michael A. Miller|title=The 68000 Microprocessor Family: Architecture, Programming, and Applications|page=47
|passage=When the microprocessor decodes the JSR opcode, it stores the operand into the TEMP '''register''' and pushes the current contents of the PC ($00 0128) onto the stack.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2014|author=Jason Gregory|title=Game Engine Architecture, Second Edition|page=90
|passage=If you can trace back through the disassembly to where the variable is first loaded into a '''register''', you can often discover its value or its address by inspecting that register.}}
# {{lb|en|printing}} The [[exact]] [[alignment]] of [[lines]], [[margins]]{{,}} and [[colors]].
# {{lb|en|printing}} The inner part of the [[mould]] in which [[type]]s are [[cast]].
# {{lb|en|music}} The [[range]] of a [[voice]] or [[instrument]].
# {{lb|en|music}} An [[organ]] [[stop]].
# {{senseid|en|language register}} {{lb|en|linguistics}} A [[style]] of a [[language]] used in a particular [[context]].
#: {{cot|en|lect}}
#: {{ux|en|We rewrote certain communications templates to use a more formal '''register'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1988|author=Andrew Radford|title=Transformational grammar: a first course|location=Cambridge, UK|publisher=Cambridge University Press|page=275|chapter=5
|passage=It seems equally clear that the ‘Complement + Prepositionʼ order illustrated in (172) (a) is likewise highly marked, and hence subject to heavy restrictions on its use. And sure enough, this does indeed seem to be the case: for one thing, forms such as ''thereafter'', ''herein'', ''whereby'' are stylistically highly marked (e.g. they are only used in particular '''registers''' such as legal language).}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2021|author=Laurel Currie Oates, Anne Enquist, Jeremy Francis|title=The Legal Writing Handbook: Analysis, Research, and Writing (8th Edition)|publisher=Wolters Kluwer|page=278|chapter=19
|passage=While e-memos are less formal than the memos discussed [above], they still need to be professional in appearance and in '''register,''' that is, in the level of formality.}}
# A [[grille]] at the [[outflow]] of a [[ventilation]] duct, capable of being opened and closed to direct the air flow.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1891|author=Anson Oliver Kittredge|title=The Metal Worker Essays on House Heating by Steam, Hot Water and Hot Air: With Introduction and Tabular Comparisons|page=22
|passage=No. 1 chamber, 1 8x12 side wall '''register''' for warm air. No. 2 chamber, 1 8x12 side wall '''register''' for warm air.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1897|author=Edward J. Mehren; Henry Coddington Meyer; John M. Goodell|title=Engineering Record, Building Record and Sanitary Engineer|page=102
|passage=The remaining ceiling '''register''' is connected with the main vent shaft containing the smokepipe. Each of the ceiling '''registers''' in the lecture hall is controlled by a damper operated by a drain in the boilerroom.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1906|title=Architectural File|page=543
|passage=The Ideal Wall '''Register''' is not a receptacle for the accumulation of dirt. It avoids the necessity of cutting carpets. It is absolutely fireproof.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1984|author=Stephen King|title=Gramma
|passage=He went up to the room he shared with Buddy and opened the hot-air '''register''' so he could hear what his mother did next.}}
# {{lb|en|mostly|US}} {{ellipsis of|en|cash register}}.

===Verb===
{{wikidata lexeme|L198}}
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[enter]] in a [[register#Noun|register]]; to [[enlist]].
#: {{syn|en|enroll|put down|Thesaurus:enlist}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[sign-up]], especially to [[vote]].
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2008|author=Barack Obama|title=[[s:Barack_Obama's_Letter_to_Vibe_Magazine|Letter to Vibe Magazine]]|passage=I am running for President to take this country in a new direction. But I can’t do it alone. I need you. Whether it’s the first time, or the first time in a long time, I need you to '''register''' and vote on November 4th.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[record]], especially in [[writing]].
#* {{RQ:London Mutiny of the Elsinore|chapter=VII|passage=In every way dinner proved up beyond my expectations, and I '''registered''' a note that the cook, whoever or whatever he might be, was a capable man at his trade.}}
# {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To [[buy]] the [[full]] version of [[trial]] software by providing one's details and payment.
#: {{ux|en|This is a trial version, and will expire in 30 days. Please '''register'''!}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[express]] [[outward]] [[sign]]s.
# {{lb|en|transitive|mail}} To record officially and [[handle]] specially.
# {{lb|en|transitive|especially|printing}} To [[make]] or [[adjust]] so as to be properly or precisely [[align]]ed.
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To place one's name, or have one's name placed in a register.
#: {{ux|en|They '''registered''' for school.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To make an [[impression]].
#* {{RQ:Rushdie Fury|page=9|passage=You’re not listening. You’ve gone off inside your head on one of your riffs and the plain fact that your son is ill hasn’t even '''registered'''. The plain fact that I have to wake up every morning and listen to him asking—unbearably asking—why his father isn’t home hasn’t '''registered'''.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To be in proper alignment; to [[align]] or [[correspond]] exactly.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1974|author=Robert Elman|title=The Hunter's Field Guide to the Game Birds and Animals of North America|isbn=9780394478876
|passage=The slightly smaller hind print may overlap but seldom '''registers''' precisely in the front track.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1992|author=Dwight R. Schuh|title=Bowhunter's Encyclopedia: Practical, Easy-to-Find Answers to Your Bowhunting Questions|publisher=Stackpole Books|isbn=9780811724128|page=279
|passage={{...}} but cat tracks are slightly more staggered, and on each side the back foot '''registers''' directly on the track of the front foot.}}
# {{lb|en|legal}} To voluntarily sign over for safe keeping, abandoning complete ownership for partial.
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[perceive]] or [[comprehend]]; [[pick up on]].
#: {{usex|en|I did not '''register''' that look to mean anything more than an innocent, friendly smile.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[occur]]; become realised or noticed; [[dawn on]].
#: {{usex|en|It did not '''register''' with me at the time that he'd end up betraying me, making off with all my savings.}}
